def: An asynchronous signal that makes a CPU suspend its current work and run a handler. NVMe controllers use interrupts to tell the host that completion queue entries are waiting.

Repeatedly checking a memory location or register for a change instead of waiting for an interrupt. In NVMe, polling means spinning on the next completion queue entry's Phase Tag; Linux uses it for poll queues and io_uring IOPOLL.
The legacy level-triggered interrupt. On PCIe it has no wires: it is emulated with Assert_INTx and Deassert_INTx message TLPs. One per function, often shared, disabled when MSI or MSI-X is enabled.
Interrupt delivered as a posted Memory Write of a host-chosen data value to a host-chosen address. Capability ID 05h; 1–32 vectors in powers of two, sharing one address.

Interrupt mechanism with a per-vector table (address, data, mask) in a BAR and a Pending Bit Array; up to 2048 vectors per function, each independently targetable and maskable. Capability ID 11h. NVMe binds each completion queue to an MSI-X vector.

Array of 16-byte entries (Message Address, Message Upper Address, Message Data, Vector Control) located in a device BAR via the MSI-X capability's Table BIR and Table Offset. Written by host software, read by the device when it signals a vector.
Fourth DWORD of an MSI-X table entry; bit 0 is the per-vector Mask Bit, set after reset. While masked, the device sets the vector's pending bit instead of sending the message.
MSI-X structure in a BAR with one read-only bit per vector, set when the device needed to signal a vector that was masked. On unmask, a pending vector is sent and its bit cleared.
The per-core interrupt controller on x86. MSI/MSI-X writes to the 0xFEEx_xxxx window are delivered to a LAPIC, which raises the CPU vector given in the message data (or via interrupt remapping).

exp: Interrupt Mask Set / Interrupt Mask Clear
def: NVMe controller registers at offsets 0Ch and 10h used to mask and unmask interrupt vectors when the controller uses pin-based (INTx) or MSI interrupts. The host must not use them when MSI-X is configured.

Delaying an interrupt so that one interrupt covers several completions. NVMe Feature 08h sets an Aggregation Threshold (0's based count) and Aggregation Time (100 µs units); Feature 09h can disable coalescing per vector.

Field in Create I/O Completion Queue (CDW11 bits 31:16) selecting the MSI-X/MSI vector the controller signals for that queue; paired with IEN (Interrupts Enabled). The admin completion queue always uses vector 0.
Bits 31:17 of completion queue entry Dword 3: Status Code, Status Code Type, Command Retry Delay, More and Do Not Retry. Zero means success.
Three-bit family of an NVMe status: 0h Generic, 1h Command Specific, 2h Media and Data Integrity Errors, 3h Path Related, 7h Vendor Specific.
Status Field bit indicating that resubmitting the same command is expected to fail. Hosts do not retry DNR completions.
NVMe log page (Log Identifier 01h) holding a ring of 64-byte error entries with Error Count, SQ ID, Command ID, status, Parameter Error Location, LBA and namespace. Pointed to by the More bit.

NVMe admin command (opcode 0Ch) the host leaves outstanding; the controller completes it when an event not tied to a command occurs (error, SMART/health, notice, command-set specific). Not to be confused with PCIe AER.
Bit 1 of the NVMe Controller Status register (offset 1Ch). Set by a controller that can no longer process commands; the host must reset it. An all-ones CSTS read is a failed PCIe read, not CFS.
A PCIe error that hardware detected and recovered from without data loss, such as Receiver Error, Bad TLP, Bad DLLP, Replay Timer Timeout or REPLAY_NUM Rollover. Signalled with ERR_COR.

A PCIe error that hardware could not correct. Classed as non-fatal (a transaction failed, link usable) or fatal (link or device untrustworthy) according to the AER Uncorrectable Error Severity register.
Correctable Data Link Layer error: the transmitter's 2-bit replay counter wrapped after repeated replays without forward progress, forcing link retraining.

A TLP whose EP (Error Poisoned) header bit is set because the sender knew its data payload was bad. The receiver logs Poisoned TLP Received and must not use the data. Different from Bad TLP (LCRC failure on the link).

Uncorrectable (default non-fatal) PCIe error logged by a requester when a non-posted request's completion does not arrive in time. The logger is usually the victim; the cause is the completer or path.
PCIe completion status (001b) and error logged by a completer that does not support or claim a request, for example an address not decoded by any BAR or an unmapped IOVA at the root complex.
Fatal-by-default PCIe error for a TLP that violates format rules, such as a payload larger than Max Payload Size or a length inconsistent with the data.
PCIe message TLPs a function sends toward the root complex to signal a correctable, uncorrectable non-fatal, or uncorrectable fatal error.
AER register (offset 04h) with one sticky write-1-to-clear bit per uncorrectable error type; shares its bit layout with the Uncorrectable Error Mask (08h) and Severity (0Ch) registers.
Four DWORDs at AER offset 1Ch holding the header of the TLP associated with the first logged uncorrectable error (the error named by the First Error Pointer).

Root port AER register (offset 30h) recording which error message classes were received, whether more than one arrived, and whether the first uncorrectable was fatal; paired with Error Source Identification (34h).
Optional PCIe capability that lets a downstream port stop traffic on its link automatically after an uncorrectable error, containing the failure before software runs.
Platform arrangement in which system firmware, not the operating system, owns AER registers, handles PCIe errors and reports them to the OS through ACPI APEI/GHES records.

The earliest observed deviation from expected behaviour, including a missing event, on a timeline merged from all evidence sources. The anchor for root-cause analysis; later events are treated as possible cascade.
